# Product Hunt

Treat Product Hunt as a concentrated product introduction and conversation, not a guaranteed ranking system. Optimize for a clear product, credible presentation, useful maker participation, and learning from the launch.

## Check fit before planning

Confirm that the product is live enough for people to try and that it is a digital product with clear utility, novelty, craft, or creativity. Verify current featuring eligibility before promising exposure. Do not build a launch plan around an unavailable product, waitlist, directory, template, course, event, or other category the current guidelines exclude.

If Product Hunt is a weak fit, say so and recommend a better role for it: a later launch milestone, feedback collection, or no launch at all.

## Gather the launch facts

Use only supported information:

- product name, URL, category, and launch version;
- target user, painful situation, and concrete outcome;
- what is usable today and how it differs from alternatives;
- pricing, access requirements, limitations, and proof;
- maker identity, origin story, and desired feedback;
- available gallery assets, demo, logo, and social proof.

Mark missing claims or assets explicitly. Never invent users, testimonials, revenue, rankings, launch history, or product capabilities.

## Build the launch strategy

Define:

- the reason to launch now;
- the specific audience that can evaluate the product;
- the product story and one primary promise;
- the listing assets required;
- the maker's role in answering questions;
- owned audiences that may be informed without asking for coordinated votes;
- success measures beyond rank, such as qualified visits, activation, feedback, or conversations;
- the follow-up decision after launch.

Do not claim that upvotes alone determine rank. Do not prescribe vote velocity targets, engagement pods, paid or incentivized votes, mass upvote requests, scripted supporter comments, or attempts to game featuring.

## Turn strategy into todos

Create finishable deliverables, not a ceremonial countdown. Typical work includes:

- verify eligibility and launch readiness;
- finalize positioning and listing copy;
- produce and review gallery or demo assets;
- draft the Maker Comment and an answer bank for likely questions;
- test the product path from listing to activation;
- prepare accurate launch announcements for existing audiences;
- monitor questions and capture feedback on launch day;
- summarize results and decide the next iteration.

Attach the evidence source, owner-ready output, and completion check to every todo. Use dates only when the project timeline supplies them.

## Write the launch package

### Tagline and description

State what the product helps a defined user do. Prefer concrete language over superlatives and category stuffing. Keep within the current Product Hunt field limits and verify those limits when publishing.

### Maker Comment

Write in the maker's real voice. Explain why the product exists, what is available now, one or two meaningful choices or lessons, and the feedback being requested. Acknowledge relevant limitations. Do not imitate community enthusiasm or manufacture a dramatic founder story.

### Gallery and demo brief

Give each asset one job: show the product, the workflow, the result, or an important distinction. Write exact screen or scene guidance and accurate captions. Do not use visuals to imply unsupported functionality.

### Announcements and replies

Share the launch with people who may genuinely care. Ask for use, feedback, or discussion—not coordinated voting. Replies must address the actual question and disclose limitations plainly. Never generate batches of generic or synthetic community comments.

## Revise without inventing momentum

Apply feedback to the named element while preserving verified facts and launch positioning. If the product has changed materially, re-check eligibility and whether the work is a new launch, an update, or a later relaunch. Verify current relaunch rules rather than assuming a fixed interval.

## Check before delivery

Confirm that:

- the product and launch type are currently eligible;
- all product claims and assets reflect what users can access;
- the package has one clear audience and product promise;
- every requested field or asset is present and usable;
- sharing language avoids vote manipulation and mass solicitation;
- mutable field limits, launch timing, and relaunch rules are verified at execution time.

Use the current official guidance when launch mechanics matter:

- Posting a product: https://help.producthunt.com/en/articles/479557-how-to-post-a-product
- Featuring guidelines: https://help.producthunt.com/en/articles/9883485-product-hunt-featuring-guidelines
- Sharing rules: https://help.producthunt.com/en/articles/2690626-how-do-i-share-my-post
- Commenting guidelines: https://help.producthunt.com/en/articles/10030102-commenting-guidelines
- Ranking points: https://help.producthunt.com/en/articles/10275873-what-are-points
- Relaunch guidance: https://help.producthunt.com/en/articles/484934-can-i-relaunch-my-product
